candidates.title: Isotope-sensitive operando signatures in TEA vs TEOA Co-bpy photocatalysis
candidates.purpose: Test whether TEA and TEOA produce different H/D-sensitive spectroscopic observables under one matched P01 configuration, consistent with different proton-coupled environments or hydrogen-containing states, while avoiding overclaim that isotope effects identify a unique intermediate.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV080 supports isotope substitution as a transferable assignment aid in operando FTIR-type measurements, not species identity in this Co-bpy system. GX010 and GX015 support proton-inventory and isotope logic as transferable discriminators of proton-delivery environments in cobalt CO2-reduction chemistry, but not direct proof for this photocatalyst. EV031 supports the transferable idea that donor or solvent environment can change detectable intermediate populations and selectivity in bipyridine-based CO2 reduction. Proposed transfer: use one preselected operando or near-operando spectroscopic mode for matched TEA and TEOA samples, compare H2O-containing and D2O-containing media within each donor, and interpret any isotope-sensitive donor difference only as evidence for differing hydrogen-coupled observables under these conditions.

comparisons.inference: Within TEOA, isotope-dependent shifts or time-course changes identify hydrogen-coupled observables worth tracking, but do not uniquely assign structure or catalytic relevance.
Within TEA, isotope-sensitive features provide the matched comparator for whether TEA accesses similar or different hydrogen-coupled observables.
Under H2O-containing conditions, donor-dependent spectral differences are descriptive only; if absent, a strong proton-management explanation is weakened but not excluded.

Under D2O-containing conditions, persistence or loss of donor-dependent signatures helps bound whether TEA and TEOA differences track hydrogen-coupled observables or remain compatible with cobalt-state and donor-redox alternatives.

This descriptive contrast helps identify donor-derived or donor-enabled features, but it is not a causal test of donor function because donor omission also changes reaction competence and solution chemistry.

procedure: Select one exact spectroscopic mode in pilot and keep it fixed for every group; if sensitivity is inadequate, move the whole card to a common fixed-delay near-operando transfer protocol rather than mixing modes.

Prepare matched TEA and TEOA P01 samples from the same cobalt source, bpy source, g-C3N4 batch, solvent family, gas handling, and optical geometry; include donor-free background if signal quality remains acceptable.

Pilot path length, catalyst loading, aqueous fraction, and acquisition timing using prespecified criteria of unsaturated spectra, repeatable baseline, and acceptable suspension scattering; reject settings that differentially degrade TEA versus TEOA baseline quality.
Acquire time-resolved spectra for all H2O-containing and D2O-containing groups under matched CO2 and illumination conditions with matched dark or pre-illumination references.
Compare reproducible band positions, intensities, and temporal profiles across groups, and relate them to parallel CO and H2 measurements only as correlation rather than mechanistic proof.
measurements: Time-resolved spectra in predefined windows classified only as candidate hydrogen-coupled, CO2-derived, ligand-associated, support-associated, or background-sensitive features
Isotope-induced shifts, attenuation, or altered temporal evolution after H2O-to-D2O substitution within each donor condition
Difference spectra against dark, pre-illumination, and donor-free references to identify background or support-derived contributions
Replicate agreement of donor-dependent isotope responses across independently prepared samples
Parallel CO and H2 product amounts from matched runs to test co-occurrence with selectivity differences without equating correlation to cause
candidates.supports: Support for H03 would be a reproducible donor-dependent isotope response under matched acquisition: TEA and TEOA differ in H/D-sensitive band positions, magnitudes, or time behavior beyond donor-free or baseline changes. Stronger but still non-decisive support occurs if donor-dependent CO and H2 divergence also changes in pattern under the same isotopic substitution.
candidates.refutes: Evidence against H03 would be that TEA and TEOA show no reproducible difference in isotope-sensitive observables under matched conditions, while spectra are dominated by shared or non-isotope-sensitive changes. If catalytic TEA and TEOA differences remain substantial in matched runs despite indistinguishable H/D-sensitive signatures, a proton-management-centered explanation is weakened relative to alternatives.
candidates.inconclusive: Inconclusive if suspension scattering or baseline drift obscures donor comparisons, if overlapping support or solvent features dominate assignment, if D2O substitution changes bulk medium properties enough that spectral differences cannot be bounded to hydrogen-coupled observables, or if donor-dependent changes are present but not isotope-sensitive.
candidates.parameter_selection: Use the literature-anchored P01 formulation family only after verifying the exact baseline composition from supplied source records. Calibrate path length, catalyst loading, aqueous fraction, and acquisition interval by pilot criteria of stable baseline, detectable catalyst-region signal, and repeatable spectra across replicate preparations. Predefine acceptable baseline-drift and scattering thresholds before comparing donors. Keep preparation order and nominal component identities matched between H2O-containing and D2O-containing groups. If pH or pD matching is attempted, document one convention and use it consistently without claiming exact equivalence.
candidates.limitations: This card can test whether TEA and TEOA differ in isotope-sensitive observables under matched conditions, but it cannot uniquely identify intermediates, prove rate-determining roles, or isolate proton management from all donor-dependent medium changes. D2O substitution is itself a multi-property perturbation, and near-operando measurements may miss the true operating state.
